pk.context: 125 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Its boxed warning for liver injury and embryo-fetal harm, under a restricted REMS program, sets this PAH endothelin blocker apart.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is about 50% and unaffected by food. Over 98% is bound to plasma proteins, mainly albumin, and it is cleared by biliary excretion after hepatic metabolism.
Molecular weight 551.6. A white to yellowish powder that is poorly soluble in water, and very stable in the solid state.
Approved under an NDA as 62.5 mg and 125 mg film-coated tablets, plus 32 mg tablets for oral suspension. Dosed twice daily.

Boxed warning for hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity under a REMS program. Contraindicated in pregnancy and with cyclosporine A or glyburide; upper respiratory tract infections and pyrexia are most common.
Pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group 1): in adults, to improve exercise ability and reduce clinical worsening; in children aged 3 and older, to improve pulmonary vascular resistance.
A specific, competitive antagonist of endothelin receptors ETA and ETB, with slightly higher affinity for ETA than for ETB.
The generic name begins with B and has eight letters.
